questions.question: Introducing a man at a birthday party, Kajal said, “This man’s son’s sister is my husband's mother.” How is Kajal’s husband related to the man?
questions.questionHtml: Introducing a man at a birthday party, Kajal said, “This man’s son’s sister is my husband's mother.” How is Kajal’s husband related to the man?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option A i.e. Grandson

Man’s son's sister means man’s daughter.

So, man’s daughter is the mother of Kajal's husband.

Thus, Kajal’s husband is the grandson of the man at the birthday party.

Hence, the correct answer is Grandson.

questions.question: In a row of girls, Shalini is 6 th from the left end and Veena is 11 th from the right end. If both interchange their position, Shalini becomes 16 th from the left end. How many girls are there in the row?
questions.questionHtml: In a row of girls, Shalini is 6<sup>th</sup> from the left end and Veena is 11<sup>th</sup> from the right end. If both interchange their position, Shalini becomes 16<sup>th</sup> from the left end. How many girls are there in the row?
questions.solution:
According to the given information,

Shalini’s position = 6th from left

Veena’s position = 11th from right

After interchanging position Shalini’s position = 16th from the left

Thus, Total girls in the row = Shalini’s position after interchanging from left + Veena’s position from right - 1

⇒ 16 + 11 - 1

⇒ 26

Hence, 26 is the correct answer.

questions.question: If SCIENCE is coded as 14 and MATHS is coded as 10, then what will be the code for EXAMINATION?
questions.questionHtml: If SCIENCE is coded as 14 and MATHS is coded as 10, then what will be the code for EXAMINATION?
questions.solution:
Here the logic is:

Total numbers of alphabets in word ⨯ 2

SCIENCE = 7 (Total numbers of alphabets) ⨯ 2 = 14

MATHS = 5 (Total numbers of alphabets) ⨯ 2 = 10

Similarly,

EXAMINATION = 11 (Total numbers of alphabets) ⨯ 2 = 22

Hence, ‘22’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: 10 cats caught 10 rats in 10 seconds. How many cats are required to catch 100 rats in 100 seconds?
questions.questionHtml: 10 cats caught 10 rats in 10 seconds. How many cats are required to catch 100 rats in 100 seconds?
questions.solution:
Given,

10 cats caught 10 rats in 10 seconds.

Cats are required to catch 100 rats in 100 seconds.

⟹ 1 cat in 10 secs caught= 1 rat

⟹ 1 cat in 100 secs caught= 10 rats

So, 10 cats can caught 100 rats in 100 seconds.

Hence, '10' is the correct answer.

Who among the following will be a righteous police officer?

options.html: An officer is ignoring a man making offensive comments to a woman.

options.text: An officer is actively participating in a violent protest.
options.html: An officer is actively participating in a violent protest.

options.text: An officer who peacefully accepted money in return for releasing a robber.
options.html: An officer who peacefully accepted money in return for releasing a robber.

options.text: An officer who ratted out another officer who was accepting bribes.
options.html: An officer who ratted out another officer who was accepting bribes.

questions.solution:
In options 1, 2, and 3, the officer is committing a crime himself:

  • by ignoring an offensive action in option 1 
  • by participating in violence in option 2 and
  • by accepting money to release a robber.


The officer who ratted out another officer for accepting bribes is the righteous police officer.

Hence option 4 is the correct answer.

Additional Information

questions.question: Read the given statement and choose the strong argument- Question: Should the government stop allowing new industries to be set up? Argument: I. Yes, new industries generate environmental pollution. II. No, new industries will improve employment and help in the economic development of the country.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the given statement and choose the strong argument-

Question:

Should the government stop allowing new industries to be set up?

Argument:

I. Yes, new industries generate environmental pollution.

II. No, new industries will improve employment and help in the economic development of the country.

options.text: Neither argument I nor argument II is strong
options.html: Neither argument I nor argument II is strong

options.text: Either Argument I or Argument II is strong
options.html: Either Argument I or Argument II is strong

questions.solution:
The question is implicitly asking whether the government should allow new industries or not.

  • Argument I suggests that the government should stop allowing new industries because they cause environmental pollution, however, it is not true. It cannot be claimed that all new industries will cause pollution. Thus, argument I is not strong.
  • Argument II talks against stopping new industries, meaning that new industries should be allowed because they help in economic development. This is a valid and strong point. Thus, argument II is strong.

Hence the correct answer is option 2.

questions.question: Mr. Sen is a hardworking labourer. He earns Rs. 250 per day. On an average he spends Rs. 75 for food, Rs.10 for dress, Rs.50 for loan repayments, Rs.10 for social service and Rs.30 for other activities on a daily basis. He deposits the balance amount in his bank account. If he takes 5 days leave in January, what will be his bank balance for the month?
questions.questionHtml: Mr. Sen is a hardworking labourer. He earns Rs. 250 per day. On an average he spends Rs. 75 for food, Rs.10 for dress, Rs.50 for loan repayments, Rs.10 for social service and Rs.30 for other activities on a daily basis. He deposits the balance amount in his bank account. If he takes 5 days leave in January, what will be his bank balance for the month?
questions.solution:
Total he earns per day = Rs. 250

His Total expenditure = (75+10+ 50+ 10+ 30) = Rs. 175 per day

January has 31 days in which he took 5 days off so money earned by him in Jan = 250 x 26 = 6500

His expenditure for 31 days = 175 x 31 = 5425

Money in his account = 6500 – 5425 = Rs. 1075

questions.question: If A denotes '+', B denotes '×', C denotes '-', and D denotes '÷', then what will come in place of '?' in the following equation? 16 D 2 B 9 C 15 A 32 = ?
questions.questionHtml:
If A denotes '+', B denotes '×', C denotes '-', and D denotes '÷', then what will come in place of '?' in the following equation?

16 D 2 B 9 C 15 A 32 = ?
questions.solution:
Explanation:

Decoding the information, 

Letter

A

B

C

D

Means

+

×

-

÷

Given:

16 D 2 B 9 C 15 A 32 = ?

After replacing the signs from left to right and using the BODMAS rule,

= 16 ÷ 2 × 9 - 15 + 32 

= 8 × 9 - 15 + 32 

= 72 - 15 + 32

= 89

Hence, “89” is the correct answer.

questions.question: If '@' denotes '×', '#' denotes '-', '$' denotes '+' and '%' denotes '÷', then, what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation? 8 $ 14 @ 5 # 56 % 7 = ?
questions.questionHtml:
If '@' denotes '×', '#' denotes '-', '$' denotes '+' and '%' denotes '÷', then, what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?

8 $ 14 @ 5 # 56 % 7 = ?
questions.solution:
BODMAS Rule:

Given:-

8 $ 14 @ 5 # 56 % 7 = ? 

Code @ # $ %
Mathematical Symbol × - + ÷

 

Replacing the codes with mathematical symbols, we get,

8 + 14 × 5 - 56 ÷ 7 = ? 

Solving using the BODMAS Rule, we get,

8 + 70 - 8 = 78 - 8 = 70

Hence, the correct answer is 70.
